unplanned_changes: S06 substitutes the original white-jacket male anchor for Senn while retaining her lance.
S05 switches Dax gauntlet to the other anatomical arm; A04 retains the correct right arm.
A01 adds a hand around the blade and secondary shoulder armor; only one clear seam dominates.
S04 changes a spear-tip shoulder stop into a blade-root/head-crest impact.
A02 keeps a low camera rather than the planned high oblique, with broadside-looking shoulder contact.
A03 shortens/simplifies the gun and loses readily visible silver forearm armor; pursuit effect resembles an ordinary energy shot.
Across components and scenes broad smooth glass plates often become intricate faceted/sharded surfaces.

comparison_to_original_full_nightglass.strengths: S01 and S06 recover the original’s strongest integrated promise: an appealing combatant, enormous inhabitable depth, a readable route and a living creature sharing the environment. S02 extends naturally into a warm dungeon discovery; S04 introduces forest depth; S05 adds a buried hall with warm ceiling light. These are substantive scene variations rather than isolated component cards.
comparison_to_original_full_nightglass.limits: Many Nightglass shadow masses are very dark at 360px art width. Face/grip/limb acceptance still requires native view. The original’s lush inhabited city shifts toward largely ruined architecture and more faceted ornament. S06 simultaneously demonstrates strong full-scene scale and direct anchor-character contamination; visual appeal does not excuse identity failure.

story_and_ecology: The fox on a safe landing and heron above floodwater give readable habitat/route relationships. The hound threatens a crossing and the long-neck Regent threatens city scale. These support the shared vocabulary; specific charge-feeding ecology and power progression are still largely conveyed by copy, not proven by still images. S04 forest and A02 city should not be presented as an unbroken chronological beat without additional transition.
